h1: Pornsiri Hotel Sisaket — A Loft-Style Bolthole in Central Sisaket That's Still Easy on the Wallet
intro: If you're heading to Sisaket and want a clean, roomy place with parking that doesn't cost a fortune, Pornsiri Hotel Sisaket is a name Isaan travellers bring up often. It's a 51-room hotel done in raw, exposed-concrete loft style, sitting in town near Rajabhat University and the Sisaket Aquarium. Guests agree on the same things: warm, hands-on owners and staff, a fresh-cooked breakfast, and rates that start at around THB 500/night.

body.html: Pornsiri Hotel Sisaket is a 51-room property in the Mueang Sisaket municipal area, styled as a loft — bare concrete walls, raw tones, paired with timber furniture for a stripped-back look with real character. Plenty of guests book on price alone and are pleasantly surprised that the rooms are roomier and cleaner than expected. Every room comes with a private balcony, which is rare at this price point in central Sisaket.

Rooms come in two main layouts — a large double bed or twin beds. They're comfortably sized, the beds are soft, the air-con is cold and the hot water runs well, with free Wi-Fi throughout. The point guests keep coming back to in reviews is cleanliness — floors, bathrooms and linens score high almost every time. Some rooms are finished in bright tones (red, yellow, green); if you'd like a particular colour, just ask at check-in.
"The room was bigger than I expected and spotlessly clean. The owner and staff were lovely and even helped sort out our transport — at this price it's superb value in Sisaket."

The real charm here is the people running it. Reviews across almost every platform mention warm, hands-on owners and staff who help with transport, point you to good local restaurants and treat guests like family. There's an on-site restaurant serving home-style dishes at fair prices, so you don't have to go far for a meal. A fresh-cooked breakfast costs around 85 baht per person, with coffee, tea, juice and rotating hot dishes.

The location is in town, near Sisaket Rajabhat University and the Sisaket Aquarium, both a few minutes' drive away. It's about 10–15 minutes by car from the city centre and the train station. The plus side is generous free parking, ideal if you're driving yourself — but it also means that without a car you'll need a Grab or local ride to reach the centre, as the area isn't very walkable.

To be straight about it, Pornsiri isn't a resort with a pool or gym. It's a friendly-priced hotel that does the basics well and completely — clean rooms, comfortable beds, easy parking, attentive hosts. For travellers coming to Sisaket on business, to visit family, or as a base before Preah Vihear / Pha Mo I Daeng, it's a sensible pick on both price and peace of mind.

The overall score sits around 7.8 from real reviews, and TripAdvisor gives it 4.5/5, placing it among the better-rated hotels in Sisaket — a fair reflection of a place that punches above its price. Just two things to know before booking: it's not bang in the city centre, and there are no big-hotel facilities. If you're fine with both, the rest is genuinely good value that's hard to find in the province.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Pornsiri Hotel Sisaket

faq.q: Where is Pornsiri Hotel Sisaket and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 249 Moo 8, Tambon Pho, Mueang Sisaket, near Sisaket Rajabhat University and the Sisaket Aquarium — both about a 5-minute drive. It's roughly 10–15 minutes by car from the train station and city centre, with free parking, making it ideal for self-drivers.

faq.q: How much does Pornsiri Hotel Sisaket cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 500/night for a Standard Double. There are also twin rooms and a Superior at about THB 650. Every room has a balcony, air-con and free Wi-Fi. Prices vary by date and platform, so compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Who is Pornsiri Hotel Sisaket best for?
faq.a: It suits self-drivers, business travellers, people visiting family, or anyone using Sisaket as a base before Preah Vihear / Pha Mo I Daeng. Clean rooms, friendly prices, attentive hosts. It's less ideal if you want a pool or a dead-centre location.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: In normal periods, 1–2 weeks ahead is fine. But on long weekends and festivals, good-value hotels like this fill up fast, so book early and pick a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't locked in.
